headline: COPPER APPROACHES $14,000/TONNE IN LONDON AS REFINED TARIFF RULING OVERDUE — U.S. STOCKPILES HIT 12-YEAR HIGH
snippet: Copper surged to the highest level in two months near $14,000 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange as U.S. import volumes hit a 12-year high — driven by pre-tariff stockpiling ahead of a White House decision on refined copper duties that missed its June 30 deadline. LME near-month copper is trading at a $370-per-tonne premium over forward contracts, the widest one-month spread since the 2021 exchange squeeze, with exchange-registered inventories falling 14% as metal is pulled toward the U.S. For junior copper explorer investors, the price signal matters: at near-$14,000 levels, advanced-stage copper porphyry projects are entering financial modelling territory that justifies full feasibility studies.

headline: GOLD SETTLES AT $4,608 WITH 5% WEEKLY GAIN — DOLLAR AT 3-MONTH LOW AS FED RATE HIKE ODDS COLLAPSE TO 31%
snippet: Spot gold settled at $4,608 per ounce on Friday August 22, posting a 5% weekly gain — its strongest weekly performance since May — as the U.S. Dollar Index hit a three-month low and Federal Reserve rate hike probability dropped from 50% to 31% following back-to-back soft inflation readings. Silver closed at $68.99, ending a week that saw the white metal briefly touch $70 intra-day. For retail investors tracking junior mining valuations, the macro setup — a weaker dollar, falling real yields, and institutional gold positioning at a 10-week high — is the most favourable combination for TSX-V and ASX gold names seen all year.

headline: USA RARE EARTH SURGES AS $500M DOE CRITICAL MINERALS GRANT FUNDS SEVEN BATTERY SUPPLY CHAIN PROJECTS
snippet: Shares of USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) jumped on Friday August 21 after the U.S. Department of Energy announced $500 million in third-round funding targeting seven projects covering critical mineral processing, battery manufacturing, and recycling capacity under President Trump's 'Unleashing American Energy' executive order. The grants continue a Washington push to onshore rare earth and critical metal supply chains that have historically depended on Chinese processing. For investors in TSX-V and ASX rare earth plays, U.S. government demand-pull — independent of commodity price — is now a meaningful re-rating catalyst for developers with projects in or near American supply chains.

headline: ARTEMIS GOLD DRILLS 259m AT 1.22 g/t AU BELOW BLACKWATER RESERVE — 85m AT 2.29 g/t HINTS AT RESOURCE EXPANSION
snippet: Artemis Gold (TSXV: ARTG) released first-drill results from its 25,000-metre resource expansion program at the producing Blackwater mine in British Columbia, with hole BWDD-26-0001 returning 259 metres at 1.22 g/t gold — including 85 metres at 2.29 g/t — below the base of the current reserve pit. Elevated silver and zinc grades in the deeper zone prompted Artemis to add a third drill rig and begin metallurgical work to evaluate zinc as a potential additional revenue stream. The discovery opens a resource expansion vector immediately below an operating mine, which reduces the development risk that typically accompanies resource additions at greenfield projects.

headline: WISDOMTREE: GOLD MINERS' CASE IS BUILDING — AISC ROSE SLOWLY AS GOLD ADDED $1,000; MARGINS AT DECADE HIGH
snippet: WisdomTree's August 20 analysis argues the fundamental case for gold mining equities has rarely been stronger: all-in sustaining costs have risen far more slowly than the gold price over the past decade, leaving producers structurally better positioned than their equity valuations imply. At gold above $4,500, senior producer free cash flow margins are at decade highs — with Newmont alone posting $2.2 billion in Q2 free cash flow — while capital returns across the sector are on pace for a record annualised $10.9 billion in dividends and buybacks in 2026. The author flags operational execution risk as the main counterforce, citing Alamos Gold's mid-year production guidance cut as a reminder that even well-run operators are not immune at any gold price.

headline: CHINA IMPORTED 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — GLOBAL VISIBLE STOCKS DOWN ~1 BILLION OZ SINCE 2021
snippet: The latest Gold SWOT analysis from US Global Investors highlights an accelerating drain on visible silver inventories: Shanghai, COMEX, and LBMA combined stocks have fallen by nearly one billion ounces since 2021, while China officially imported over 790 tonnes of silver in the first months of 2026 — largely for solar panel manufacturing after Beijing reclassified silver as a strategic material in January 2026. The simultaneous drawdown across all three major exchange warehouses signals that above-ground supply is being absorbed faster than mine production and recycling can replace it. For retail investors in TSX-V and ASX silver juniors, the structural inventory deficit at $68–$70 spot silver is the supply-side thesis playing out in real time.

headline: URANIUM SPOT HOLDS $88.85/LB — KAZATOMPROM H1 OUTPUT +9%, DENISON PHOENIX ISR ENTERS FULL-SCALE CONSTRUCTION
snippet: Uranium spot held near $88.85 per pound as Kazatomprom — the world's largest producer — reported a 9% year-on-year increase in Kazakhstan's uranium output for the first half of 2026, adding to global supply at a time when AI data centre operators and governments are driving power demand toward nuclear. Separately, Denison Mines confirmed that civil works are more than 20% complete at the Wheeler River Phoenix In-Situ Recovery project in northern Saskatchewan, with approximately 400 workers on site and first production targeted for mid-2028. Phoenix — Canada's first commercial ISR uranium mine — uses a freeze-wall containment system that eliminates conventional mining excavation, lowering capital intensity versus peer projects.

headline: LITHIUM CARBONATE +78% IN ONE MONTH IN CHINA; COBALT +130% ON DRC EXPORT RESTRICTIONS — IEA 2026 DATA
snippet: The IEA's Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026 and Credendo's concurrent market update document twin price shocks in the battery metals complex: lithium carbonate prices in China surged 78.3% in just over one month — reaching the highest level since late 2023 — after Beijing reduced VAT export rebates on lithium-ion batteries from April 1, prompting a front-loading rush; cobalt jumped roughly 130% after the Democratic Republic of the Congo imposed export restrictions on refined cobalt. Despite the price recovery, capital spending on lithium fell approximately 40% year-over-year as miners remain cautious after 2023–2024 oversupply losses. The divergence between recovering prices and contracting capex sets up a supply-deficit cycle for mid-decade that could benefit advanced lithium developers.

headline: EVOLUTION MINING ADDS COPPER TO GROWTH PIPELINE — GOLD SWOT: ASX PRODUCERS DIVERSIFYING INTO COPPER AT SCALE
snippet: This week's Gold SWOT from US Global Investors highlights Evolution Mining's move to expand its copper growth pipeline as representative of a broader trend: senior gold producers are diversifying into copper at scale, aligning with near-$6.60-per-pound copper and long-term EV and grid electrification demand, while retaining gold as the primary revenue driver. The pattern reflects a capital allocation shift among senior and mid-tier producers who are using record gold free cash flow to fund copper-adjacent exploration and acquisition programs. For investors in TSX-V and ASX juniors, producer-level appetite for copper validates the strategic rationale for advanced-stage copper-gold developers in established jurisdictions.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER EXPANDS MOROCCAN EXPLORATION FOOTPRINT — NEW DRILL TARGETS ADDED TO ZGOUNDER DISTRICT
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver (TSX: AYA) has expanded its exploration footprint at the Zgounder Silver Mine district in Morocco, adding new drill targets to its 2026 exploration program alongside the operating mine. Zgounder is among the highest-grade primary silver mines operating globally, with recent production expansions making Aya a rare TSX-listed producing silver company with near-mine discovery upside. The move was highlighted in GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT as illustrative of a growing pattern among profitable silver producers: deploying operating cash flow from elevated spot prices into district-scale exploration to extend mine life and support resource re-ratings.

headline: U.S. COPPER IMPORTS HIT 12-YEAR HIGH, CUTTING LME INVENTORIES 14% AND WIDENING DELIVERY PREMIUMS
snippet: Pre-tariff copper stockpiling has driven U.S. import volumes to a 12-year high, pulling metal off LME exchange-registered inventories and widening delivery premiums to levels last seen in the 2021 copper squeeze. Spot copper is trading at over $543 per tonne above the three-month forward contract — the widest near-term premium spread in years — as a potential refined copper tariff remains unsigned past the June 30 Commerce Department deadline. The stockpiling dynamic creates a dual-headline risk: a tariff announcement could trigger unwinding of U.S. inventory positions, while continued delay sustains LME tightness and keeps prices near $14,000 per tonne.

headline: GOLD PRICE SET TO CRACK $4,700 — GEOPOLITICAL AND MONETARY RISKS REMAIN ELEVATED IN H2 2026: CRUX INVESTOR
snippet: Crux Investor's latest gold outlook argues that gold is priced toward $4,700 per ounce in the second half of 2026, underpinned by persistent geopolitical risk, a structurally weaker U.S. dollar, and fiscal sustainability concerns that have pushed institutional gold positioning to multi-month highs. The piece highlights gold's five consecutive weeks of gains and flags the Treasury's surprise expansion of longer-dated bond purchases as a catalyst likely to keep real yields suppressed — the most reliable medium-term predictor of gold price direction. For retail investors, a move toward $4,700 implies additional headroom that could further re-rate TSX-V and ASX junior gold equities from their current discounts to net asset value.
